# task-7189c874: copy the marked panel into every equal panel

## Validated rule

Identify complete, uniform divider rows and/or columns that partition the grid into equally sized panels. Find the panel that contains the pattern/foreground marks against an otherwise uniform background; that is the source panel, and it need not be the bottom-right panel. Copy the source panel's entire contents by direct positional alignment into every panel, including the source's blank/background cells. Preserve all divider cells and output the original dimensions. Do not reflect or rotate the source.

Confirmed by one demo and one accepted test in this task:

- Demo (15x11): a full divider column (color 1) and divider row (color 1) partition the grid into four equal 7x5 panels. The top-right panel contains a sparse pattern on background 8; the other panels are blank. The output repeats the top-right panel's entire pattern into all four panels, preserving dividers. This directly shows that the source is the marked panel, not necessarily bottom-right.
- Accepted test (23x5): divider column 2 (color 2) and divider rows 7 and 15 (color 2) make six 7x2 panels. The middle-right panel (rows 8–14, cols 3–4, 0-indexed) contains marks on background 1. The accepted output copies this whole 7x2 panel into all six panels by local coordinates; divider lines remain unchanged. Thus the source can be in the middle band, and the pattern replicates both across rows and across columns.

## Application checks

1. Verify the full uniform divider lines and equal panel dimensions.
2. Locate the uniquely marked/non-background panel; do not assume it is bottom-right. If more than one distinct marked panel makes the source ambiguous, request a demo.
3. Copy every source-panel cell to the same local coordinate in every panel, including background values, and preserve divider cells.
4. Verify dimensions and row lengths. Avoid merely repeating marks in the source column/band: copy the whole panel across the entire partition.

## Additional accepted instance

A 13x13 test had uniform divider row 6 and divider column 6, both color 4, producing four 6x6 panels. The top-right panel was the uniquely marked panel, on background 2. Its complete 6x6 contents (including background cells) were copied positionally into all four panels, preserving the divider cross and the original 13x13 dimensions.
